predecessors.name: Kara-Khanid Khanate
predecessors.text: the Eastern Khanate, 'capital at Balasaghun and later Kashgar'

successors.name: Qara Khitai (Western Liao)
successors.text: the Tarim Basin part of the Eastern shape: Kashgar, Yarkand, Khotan, Aksu and Kucha, the 'Kashgar (1130-1211)' of the infobox

ledger.x: 1046: the Eastern Khanate of the Kara-Khanids is formed at Balasagun.
1066: the Fergana valley passes to the Western Khanate.
1087: Malik-Shah's Seljuks invade the Karakhanid lands as far as the Eastern Khanate.
1089: the Eastern khan is a Seljuk vassal and the campaign is over.
1089: the Eastern Khanate is a Seljuk vassal.
1096: Kucha, Aksu and Tumshuk are in Kara-Khanid hands.
1130: the Eastern capital moves from Balasagun to Kashgar.
1134: Yelü Dashi takes Balasagun and the Chu valley.
1141: the Eastern Khanate, left at Kashgar, becomes a Qara Khitai vassal.
1204: the Qara Khitai put down a rebellion at Kashgar.
1204: the Kashgar rebellion is suppressed and the Qara Khitai overlordship stands.
1211: the vassalage ends when the Eastern prince is killed at Kashgar by the rebels.

wars.name: Seljuk campaign into Talas and Zhetysu
wars.outcome: Seljuk victory: the Eastern khan Hasan ibn Suleiman submits at Uzkand and the Karakhanids of Kashgar 'declared their submission'; the vassalage lasts 'only a short time'.

wars.name: Qara Khitai conquest of the Eastern Khanate
wars.outcome: Dashi is repelled at Kashgar in the summer of 1131, takes Balasagun in 1134 and, 'after 1137', Kashgar, Khotan and Beshbalik; the Karakhanid dynasty stays in power at Kashgar as Qara Khitai vassals from 1141.

wars.name: Kashgar rebellion against the Qara Khitai
wars.outcome: The rebellion of 1204 is suppressed; the last Eastern prince is released and killed at Kashgar by rebels in 1211, ending the khanate.

certainty.note: Steppe, mountain and oasis frontiers throughout, no survey or treaty line; the Fergana-Zhetysu border with the Western Khanate was 'frequently contested'.
